The card sums 1 over each degree, 1/3 + 1/2, for a resource allocation index of 0.833." width="100%"} For each pair of nodes `(u, v)`, computes `Σ(1 / |N(w)|)` for all common neighbors `w`. Similar to Adamic-Adar but uses `1/degree` instead of `1/log(degree)`, penalizing high-degree common neighbors more strongly. A shared neighbor of degree 2 contributes `0.5`, while a hub of degree 100 contributes only `0.01`. The graph is not modified. Resource allocation is a strong local link-prediction score, useful for: - recommending connections when hubs (popular pages, large institutions) should count for very little - ranking candidate links in networks with heavy-tailed degree distributions - comparing against `adamic_adar_index()` to see how sensitive a ranking is to the hub penalty The measure is intended for undirected graphs. On a directed graph, neighbors and degrees are taken from *outgoing* edges, and a shared neighbor with out-degree `0` contributes nothing. When `ebunch=` is `None`, every pair of non-adjacent nodes is scored, which is quadratic in the number of nodes; pass `ebunch=` on large graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of `(u, v)` node pairs to score. Each node can be given as a node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). Pairs are scored even if `u` and `v` are already connected, and they are returned in the order given. If `None` (the default), all pairs of nodes that are not already connected (in either direction) are scored, each unordered pair once, in no particular order. A node that doesn't exist raises a `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(u, v, index)` tuples where index is the resource allocation score (`0.0` when the nodes share no neighbors). Nodes are reported as node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node in `ebunch=` does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Resource allocation shares its shape with Adamic-Adar but replaces $1/\log|N(w)|$ with the harsher $1/|N(w)|$: $\mathrm{RA}(u, v) = \sum_{w \in N(u) \cap N(v)} \dfrac{1}{|N(w)|}$. The motivating picture is a unit of resource sent from $u$ to $v$ that splits evenly at each hub $w$ before arriving; a rarer hub delivers a larger fraction. That heavier hub penalty frequently edges out Adamic-Adar on social-network link-prediction benchmarks. Runs in $O(k)$ per pair. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star with hub `1` and nine leaves, any two leaves share only the hub, which has degree 9. Resource allocation scores each such pair `1/9`, about `0.11`, noticeably lower than Adamic-Adar's `1/ln(9)`, about `0.46` (shown first in each pair): ::: {#f9113432 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node() # hub, node 1 for i in range(2, 11): graph.add_node() graph.add_edge(1, i) pairs = [(2, 3), (2, 5)] list(zip(graph.adamic_adar_index(pairs), graph.resource_allocation_index(pairs))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [((2, 3, 0.45511961331341866), (2, 3, 0.1111111111111111)), ((2, 5, 0.45511961331341866), (2, 5, 0.1111111111111111))] ``` ::: ::: With labelled nodes, the penalty on hubs is easy to see. `Ann` and `Bob` share one contact of degree 2 (score `1/2`), while `Cat` and `Dan` share two hubs of degree 8 (score `2/8`), so resource allocation ranks `Ann`/`Bob` first even though `Cat`/`Dan` have more common neighbors: ::: {#5b601179 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_nodes(["Ann", "Bob", "Kim", "Cat", "Dan", "H1", "H2"]) graph.add_nodes([f"x{i}" for i in range(12)]) graph.add_edge("Ann", "Kim").add_edge("Bob", "Kim") for hub in ["H1", "H2"]: graph.add_edge("Cat", hub).add_edge("Dan", hub) for i in range(6): graph.add_edge(hub, f"x{i}" if hub == "H1" else f"x{i + 6}") graph.resource_allocation_index([("Ann", "Bob"), ("Cat", "Dan")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [(1, 2, 0.5), (4, 5, 0.25)] ``` ::: :::
